long_biography.plain_text:
Island Tug & Barge was established in Seattle by Norm and Wanda Stanley in 1979. Frank Ellefsen and Dave Wells worked in the business for years before acquiring it together in 2010. That transition made Ellefsen an operating owner of a company already embedded in the region's commercial marine trade. A Washington state labour ruling subsequently addressed him as its president during a question about wages for tugboat work on a river-cleanup project.

The Seattle operator's tugs and barges serve quite different assignments: moving raw materials, supporting dredging and construction, and towing along the Pacific coast and to Alaska. Its barge fleet can be chartered for specialised cargoes as well as routine freight. The company maintains its working base on the Duwamish waterway. Ellefsen's professional story is grounded in the transition from an established employee to a partner responsible for a fleet-based transport service.
